rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Summary 2 Game Setup 3 Game Play 4 Game End 5 Settings 5.1 Placement Hints 5.2 Drag and drop Summary Each round there are four new shapes to place in each of the junk drawer compartments. Each compartment can be used only once per round. Most points at game end wins! Game Setup A goal card is dealt out for each of the junk drawer grids, showing how a player can score points in each. Game Play Each round a player has to place the shape in a junk drawer, trying to maximize their score as outlined in the goal cards. (Note everyone places the shape on their own board.) To place the shape, tap/click on the grid, and to move, tap/click a new position. You can use the buttons to rotate or flip. Click "Confirm" to confirm, and when all players have placed their shape then the game moves to the next shape or to the next round. (You may be able to change placement preferences in settings.) Game End A player must pass if they can't place a shape. (They will not have an option to pass if there is a shape they can play.) The game continues until one (or all) player(s) can't place a shape. When each player has placed that shape (or passed) the game ends. If you are playing in solo mode, you need to gain more points than the combined example scores shown on the goal cards to win. A game variation keeps the game going until the last player passes. Settings Placement Hints There is a user preference that will give you a help button which will indicate where a shape can be placed. The intention is that experienced players will choose not to use this, but it is there in case you just can't find a location for a shape. Drag and drop The default option for placing shapes is to tap and click but this can be changed to drag and drop in player preferences. Drag and drop does not work properly on touch screens.

[Rating: 3/10] an extremely bland game, fit the pieces in your personal board, score points at the end. MPS with no interesting choices

[Rating: 3/10] Tile placement game. Four different parts of the board, each one with a different scoring rule.  More of the same.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Polyomino IV: Return Of The Space - The Board Game  I’m convinced there is a yearly quota for these type of games, you have a piece and you must fit said piece on a board (this time its one of four). You get points based on the criteria they provide, slap a “1-4 players” label on it and call it a game. Bonus points if you include a makeshift theme.  Side Note: I’m part of the problem as I will always play these games at least once. Just a hopeless romantic when it comes to “tetris-like” games.

[Rating: 4/10] Fully solitaire flip-and-write-esque simultaneous puzzle boarding. Inoffensive and quick, but not my kind of "game".

[Rating: 4/10] I just don't have the brain for these games of positioning jigsaw pieces, although I do enjoy the difficult decisions this one forces player into with its Biblios-esque requirement to assign an item to each drawer, one at a time, before they are all known.
